---
title: "4 Reliability and agreement studies"
link-citations: true
---

Alternative labels: reproducibility as a special type of agreement study

## Definition and features
In reliability and agreement studies, researchers ask multiple users, teams, or artificial intelligence systems to apply the same method to the same set of cases, usually studies or datasets. Researchers may use an existing set of cases or create a new set specifically for the study. They then assess consistency across applications using measures of reliability, which show how well ratings distinguish cases across users, or measures of agreement, which show how similar ratings or results are across users. Reproducibility studies are a special case of agreement studies in which independent teams try to obtain the same results as the original study team by re-running the same statistical workflow on the same data.

- A strength of these studies is that they quantify variability introduced by method users.
- A challenge is that results depend on case difficulty and user experience, and consistency does not necessarily indicate correctness.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="minimal" collapse="true"}
## Boundaries with related types
[Experimental analysis of real datasets](3real-datasets.qmd):
Both may use a single dataset and assess agreement, but reliability and agreement studies compare users applying the same method, whereas experimental analyses compare methods applied by one user or team.
:::

## Typical purposes and corresponding examples 
[Evaluate a single method](../purposes/7evaluate-method.qmd): Reliability of risk of bias tools for observational studies;[@Kalaycioglu2023inter-rater] Reliability of 12 raters applying a quality assessment tool for radiomics to 35 studies and repeated the assessment after a wash-out period.[@AkinciDAntonoli2025reproducibility] Agreement between nine research teams attempting to reproduce the same observational study;[@Ostropolets2023reproducible] Agreement between reproduced and original analyses of 150 real-world evidence studies.[@Wang2022reproducibility]
